problems.problem: The ground still renders as glossy veined marble tiles: the contact crop (62,1069,585,1319) and the full poster both show a square tile grid with grout seams and reflective sheen under the base, directly contradicting the declared 'continuous matte honed pale limestone, no tiles, no grout lines'. The tiled foreground reads as室内 flooring stock, not the courtyard mineral plane of the concept, and its cool gloss fights the matte ultramarine plaster.

The sundial shadow edge regressed: the previous version at least showed a hard wedge at the top-left; the current wall carries only a faint soft diagonal tonal drift across the upper third with no crisp terminator. The declared 'one broad hard diagonal shadow edge raking from upper left' is not legible, so the wall reads as flat unmodulated blue and the core light idea of the concept is missing.

Contact is real (crop proves the base meets the ground at y=1209 with a soft ambient pool; offset_y 0 is correct, keep it), but the shadow story is inconsistent: the pool is neutral and omnidirectional while the concept declares hard raking sun, and the cutout retains soft frontal-top studio speculars. With no cast shadow direction on the ground and no crisp sun edge on the wall, the flacon still reads as a pasted cutout rather than a body standing in sunlight.

The foreground floor band (y approx 1210-1440, roughly 16% of canvas) remains dead space: glossy empty tiles holding nothing but faint sheen, while the bottle base sits almost exactly on the wall/ground junction. References (Hermes branch shadow, Sisley stepped stone and botanicals) let the ground plane carry shadow, texture and depth; here the product is pinned to the horizon line and the patio below it is vacant.

The right column still does not close: after the two-line title ending near y=797 there is a ~140 px void before 'EAU DE PARFUM' at y=940 and the gold rule at y=1000, leaving the column visually top-loaded and the zone beside the bottle body and label empty; the rule floats mid-wall instead of anchoring the column toward the bottle base line.

changes.value: Seamless matte honed pale limestone ground as one continuous mineral plane with fine grain, no tiles, no grout lines, no seams, no veining, meeting a deep ultramarine lime-washed plaster wall at a low horizon; one broad crisp diagonal shadow terminator raking the wall from upper left across a third of its height and continuing as a soft angled shade across the ground; warm low direct sunlight grazing the mineral grain, empty scene, no objects
